Project instructions

FileScope
$ORCA_CONFIG_DIR/AGENTS.mdEvery workspace on this machine.
<workspace>/AGENTS.mdThis project.
<workspace>/.orca/AGENTS.mdThis checkout, unshared.

All applicable files are read at startup (up to 32 kB each) and appended to the system prompt. A live user request takes precedence. Changes appear on the next session, or after /clear in a running session.

Skill roots and precedence

Orcacode scans project locations before user locations, so a repository can provide its own procedure without asking contributors to move their existing skills.

Root orderLocations
Project first.orca/skills, skills, .claude/skills, .agents/skills, .codex/skills, .opencode/skills
Then user$ORCA_CONFIG_DIR/skills, then compatible roots under ~

When two valid skills share a name, the earlier root wins and the later copy appears as shadowed in /skills. A malformed skill is reported but does not stop other skills from loading.

Author and install skills

› /skills create release
› /skills create release --global
› /skills add owner/repo --skill release
› /skills add owner/repo --here
› /skills reload

/skills create writes a starter skill to .orca/skills; use --global for the config-directory skill folder. /skills add installs into the managed config folder by default; --here installs into the project. Read an installed skill before enabling it: the body is instruction text the agent can follow.

Skill format

A skill is a directory containing SKILL.md. Its frontmatter requires a description; the name is optional and defaults to the directory name. Names may use letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, and periods.

---
name: release
description: Prepare and verify a release
---

Read the version, run the release checks, and report the evidence.

Use /skills show <name> to inspect discovery state and /skills remove <name> to delete skills Orcacode installed. It will not delete a compatibility skill owned by another tool.

Load a skill

Use /skills to list and toggle discovered skills. During a task, the agent uses the skill tool to load a skill’s instructions and named resources before it starts work. A $skill-name mention in your prompt explicitly asks it to load that enabled skill.
